title: Foundations: Gospel Worship - The Complete Guide
summary: What Gospel Worship is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Gospel Worship songs: Gospel choir music is massed voices in praise: sopranos soaring, altos answering, tenors testifying, over piano, organ, and drums. The choir is both instrument and congregation.

History: Thomas A. Dorsey — the father of gospel music — fused blues with church hymns in Chicago in the 1930s. The Roberta Martin Singers, the Edwin Hawkins Singers (Oh Happy Day, 1969), and Kirk Franklin brought choir gospel to pop charts.

How the songs work: Gospel Worship favors the keys of Ab, Bb, Eb, F, G. Common forms include Verse-chorus with a repeated vamp that builds; Call-and-response between leader and choir. Players should master the vamp: repeat a two-chord loop, adding voices each time first, then modulation up a half step for the final chorus. Pianists rule here; guitarists use barre shapes.

title: Amazing Grace - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Amazing Grace, a public-domain Gospel Worship standard.
body:
Amazing Grace (Words by John Newton, 1779; tune NEW BRITAIN (1835). Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Amazing grace! how sweet the sound
That saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
Was blind, but now I see.

'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How precious did that grace appear
The hour I first believed!

Through many dangers, toils, and snares,
I have already come;
'Tis grace hath brought me safe thus far,
And grace will lead me home.

When we've been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We've no less days to sing God's praise
Than when we'd first begun.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Gospel Worship accompaniment in Ab using the 'Praise I–IV–V' pattern:
G# | C# | D# | G#

Technique: the vamp: repeat a two-chord loop, adding voices each time. Pianists rule here; guitarists use barre shapes.

Swing low, sweet chariot,

I looked over Jordan, and what did I see,

Coming for to carry me home;
Tell all my friends I'm coming too,
